/article/detail/29.html.title: Shenzhen MSU-BIT University
/article/detail/29.html.summary: Located in the Shenzhen International University Park in the southwest of Universiade New City, Longgang District, adjacent to the CUHK (Shenzhen) campus. Site area 334,000 m², planned floor area 279,568 m², investment 1.78 billion yuan.
/article/detail/29.html.bodyHtml:
Shenzhen MSU–BIT University is located in Shenzhen International University Park, southwest of Universiade New Town in Longgang District, next to The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen. The campus occupies 334,000 m², with a planned floor area of 279,568 m² and an investment of RMB 1.78 billion.

Designed with high standards, consistency and a forward-looking approach, the campus draws on leading international university design principles. It combines a considered layout, landscaped surroundings and comprehensive functions with a distinctive Russian architectural style. Leaders of China and Russia visited the project, a milestone in educational and cultural cooperation between the two countries.

The steel spire stands at the center of the main building and comprises the tower body, internal stairs and a five-pointed star. The circular platforms at elevations of 114 m and 146 m have diameters of 7.25 m and 3.1 m respectively. The spire structure is 56.05 m tall, and its tip is 156.4 m above ground.

/article/detail/85.html.title: Cumark Tower
/article/detail/85.html.summary: One of Guangdong Province's first prefabricated construction demonstration projects and a Shenzhen engineering construction technology demonstration project — Shenzhen's first high-rise built with the assembled steel structure light-panel building system under the EPC model. Floor area 38,697 m², 17 floors above ground.
/article/detail/85.html.bodyHtml:
Cumark Tower was among Guangdong's first prefabricated building demonstration projects and is a Shenzhen construction science and technology demonstration project.

Delivered by GSIN under an EPC contract, the project is described in the original records as Shenzhen's first high-rise using a prefabricated steel-structure light-panel building system, the city's first EPC prefabricated steel-structure project, and its first three-star green prefabricated steel-structure project. It hosted project observation visits for Guangming New District and China Construction Seventh Engineering Division in 2017.

Designed to China's three-star green building standard, the project uses a prefabricated steel-structure light-panel building system jointly developed with the China Academy of Building Research, Tsinghua University and Chongqing University.

Located in Guangming New District's technology industrial park, the project occupies 7,654 m², with a total floor area of approximately 40,000 m², two basement levels and 17 above-ground storeys. The original narrative gives a building height of 69.9 m. The above-ground structure is entirely steel, using approximately 2,200 tonnes. Exterior and interior walls use high-performance autoclaved lightweight concrete (ALC) panels; floors use steel-bar truss decking, and the curtain wall uses an insulating low-E energy-saving system.

/article/detail/294.html.title: Qiufu Prefabricated Heavy-Steel Villa
/article/detail/294.html.summary: Located in Meizhou, Guangdong Province, with heavy steel as the main frame and a composite wall of dry-hung ceramic panels + ALC wall panels as the cladding system. Seismic fortification intensity 9 degrees; withstands force-17 typhoons.
/article/detail/294.html.bodyHtml:
Located in Meizhou, Guangdong, the villa uses a heavy-steel main frame. Its building envelope consists of composite walls combining dry-hung terracotta panels and ALC wall panels.

The original project description states a seismic fortification intensity of 9 degrees and resistance to force-17 typhoons, and describes advantages over conventional brick-and-concrete construction in thermal insulation, heat resistance, sound insulation and environmental performance.
